tested_scope: Exactly one deterministic self-local positive-control replay continuing the immediately preceding reservation/effect ambiguity fixture. The replay assumes a stable logical effect identity effect:E, a fixed payload P, a current-authority/fence predicate checked immediately before every external effect attempt and local marker write, and an intrinsically idempotent durable effect primitive apply_once(effect:E,P) whose first accepted call performs the useful external effect once and durably binds the result to effect:E, while every later same-key/same-payload call returns the bound result without performing a second external effect. The local done marker remains nontransactional with the external effect. The replay covers a crash after the external effect is accepted but before the local done marker, followed by a legitimate authority-turnover retry with the same stable effect key, plus a stale-old-claimant resume after turnover. No concrete transport, public source, O/downstream/other-worker state, shared ledger, scheduler mutation, hosted compute, richer-mode arbitration, finite quota, or optional second semantic leaf is modeled.

fixture.protocol_under_test: current-authority check -> apply_once(stable_effect_key,payload) -> nontransactional local done marker
positive_control_schedule: A0 is current, passes the authority/fence predicate, and has no local done marker for effect:E.
A0 calls apply_once(effect:E,P); the primitive accepts the call, performs the useful external effect exactly once, and durably binds its result to effect:E.
A0 crashes after the external effect/result binding but before writing the local done marker.
Authority legitimately turns over to A1.
A1 passes the then-current authority/fence predicate, observes the local done marker still absent, and retries apply_once(effect:E,P).
The retry returns the already-bound result for effect:E and performs no second external effect.
A1 writes the local done marker after rechecking current authority/fence.
If stale A0 later resumes, it fails the current authority/fence predicate before any further effect attempt or marker write.

observations: Replacing an ambiguous local reservation marker with a durable effect-side idempotency key removes the specific crash-after-effect-before-local-marker duplicate window in this tested history: the legitimate retry is allowed, but the external effect count remains one.

The authority/fence predicate and the effect idempotency key solve different failure classes: fencing rejects stale actors after turnover, while the stable effect key collapses repeated attempts by legitimate current actors after an unknown local completion state.

The local done marker can lag the external effect without forcing a duplicate in this model because duplicate suppression is anchored at the effect primitive rather than inferred from local marker state.
inference: Within this exact abstract model, current-authority fencing plus a durable intrinsically idempotent effect primitive keyed by stable logical effect identity is sufficient to prevent duplicate external effects across the tested crash-after-effect-before-local-marker and legitimate authority-turnover retry history without transactional coupling to the local marker. This is only a conditional positive control: it does not prove that any allowed Chat-exposed primitive provides durable apply-once semantics, does not test same-key/different-payload or key-reuse/ABA behavior, and does not by itself prove eventual liveness or no-loss if repeated crashes prevent any effect attempt from being durably accepted.
unresolved_children: A concrete allowed zero-cost quota-independent Chat-exposed primitive that exposes durable stable-key idempotency together with current-authority validation remains unverified.

Same-key/different-payload rejection and logical-key reuse or ABA across distinct effect generations have not been replayed; a bad key discipline could convert safe duplicate suppression into false suppression of a distinct intended effect.

Eventual no-loss/liveness under crash-before-first-accept and repeated retry interruption remains untested; this positive control establishes duplicate safety only for the exact accepted-first-effect history above.
